    Comparison theorems

    Space forms

    Edit

    In applications, comparison theorems are mainly used to compare a given manifold with a space form of constant sectional curvature, in order to obtain suitable estimates. For this purpose, we first consider the Hessian of the distance function on a space form.

    Let \(\overline{M}(K_0)\) be an \(m\)-dimensional space form of constant sectional curvature \(K_0\), endowed with the metric \(g\). In geodesic polar coordinates

    \[ (r,\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^{m-1}) \]

    centered at a point \(O\in \overline{M}(K_0)\), the metric \(g\) takes the form

    \[ g=(dr)^2+f(r)^2\,d\sigma^2, \]

    where

    \[ d\sigma^2 = h_{ij}(\theta)\,d\theta^i d\theta^j, \qquad 1\le i,j\le m-1, \]

    is the standard metric on the unit sphere \(\mathbb{S}^{m-1}\).

    The radial function \(f(r)\) satisfies

    \[ \begin{cases} f''+K_0f=0,\\ f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=1. \end{cases} \]

    Hence,

    \begin{equation} \label{1} f(r)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sin(\sqrt{K_0}\,r)}{\sqrt{K_0}}, & K_0>0,\quad r<\dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{K_0}}, \\ r, & K_0=0, \\ \dfrac{\sinh(\sqrt{-K_0}\,r)}{\sqrt{-K_0}}, & K_0<0. \end{cases} \end{equation}

    Proposition
    Edit

    The distance function \(\rho \) on \(\overline{M}(K_0)\) can be expressed as

    \begin{equation} \hess(\rho )=\frac{f'(\rho )}{f(\rho )}(g-d \rho \otimes d\rho ), \end{equation}

    where \(f\) is defined by \eqref{1}.

    Example
    Edit

    The distance function from the original point on Euclidean space \(\rr^m\) is given by

    \[ \rho (x)=\sqrt{x_{1}^{2}+\cdots +x_{m}^{2}}. \]

    Thus

    \[ \rho _i = \frac{x_i}{\rho } , \qquad \rho _{ij}= \frac{\delta _{ij}}{\rho }-\frac{x_i x_j}{\rho ^3}. \]

    For a vector field \(\xi \in T_x \rr^m\),

    \[ \begin{aligned} \hess(\rho )(\xi ,\xi )=& \rho _{ij} \xi ^i \xi ^j=\frac{|\xi |^2}{\rho }-\frac{\la x, \xi \ra^2}{\rho ^3}\\ =& \frac{1}{\rho }(g-d \rho \otimes d \rho )(\xi ,\xi ) . \end{aligned} \]

    When \(\xi \perp \frac{\partial }{\partial \rho }\),

    \[ \hess(\rho )(\xi ,\xi )= \frac{|\xi |^2}{\rho }; \]

    when \(\xi =\frac{\partial }{\partial \rho }\),

    \[ \hess(\rho )(\xi ,\xi )=0. \]

    Comparison theorems

    Edit

    Let \(M\) be a complete Riemannian manifold, and let \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\) denote the Riemannian metric. Fix a point \(O\in M\). For any \(p\in M\), define

    \[ \rho(p)=\rho(O,p), \]

    where \(\rho\) is the distance function from \(O\). This is one of the most natural and important functions on a Riemannian manifold. We now consider the Hessian of the distance function.

    On the neighborhood

    \[ \exp_O(E_O)\subset M \]

    of \(O\) on which the exponential map \(\exp_O\) is defined, introduce geodesic polar coordinates

    \[ (r,\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^{m-1}). \]

    In these coordinates, the metric \(g\) on \(M\) takes the form

    \[ g = (dr)^2 + f(r)^2 h_{ij}(r,\theta)\,d\theta^i d\theta^j, \qquad 1\le i,j\le m-1, \]

    where \(f(r)\) is a nonnegative radial function.

    Let

    \[ p\in \exp_O(E_O) \]

    be a point which is not a cut point of \(O\). Then there exists a unique minimizing unit-speed geodesic

    \[ \gamma(t) \]

    joining \(O\) to \(p\), such that

    \[ \gamma(0)=O, \qquad \gamma(r)=p. \]

    Consequently,

    \[ \rho(p)=r. \]

    Definition
    Edit

    Let \(M\), \(O\), \(\rho\), and \(\gamma\) be as above. If a two-dimensional plane

    \[ \pi_p\subset T_pM \]

    contains the radial vector

    \[ \frac{\partial}{\partial r}(p), \]

    then \(\pi_p\) is called a radial plane. The sectional curvature of a radial plane is called the radial curvature.

    Theorem (Hessian Comparison Theorem)
    Edit

    Let \(M_k\) \((k=1,2)\) be two \(m\)-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, and let

    \[ \gamma_k:[0,r]\to M_k \]

    be geodesics parametrized by arc length such that \(\gamma_k(r)\) is not a cut point of \(\gamma_k(0)\). Let \(\rho_k\) denote the distance function on \(M_k\) from \(\gamma_k(0)\), for \(k=1,2\).

    Assume that the radial curvature of \(M_1\) along \(\gamma_1\) is greater than or equal to the radial curvature of \(M_2\) along \(\gamma_2\). Then

    \[ \operatorname{Hess}(\rho_1)(X_1,X_1) \le \operatorname{Hess}(\rho_2)(X_2,X_2), \]

    where

    \[ X_k\in T_{\gamma_k(r)}M_k, \qquad k=1,2, \]

    satisfy

    \[ \left\langle X_1,\frac{\partial}{\partial r_1} \right\rangle_{M_1} = \left\langle X_2,\frac{\partial}{\partial r_2} \right\rangle_{M_2}, \]

    and

    \[ \|X_1\|=\|X_2\|. \]

    Corollary
    Edit

    Under the same assumptions as in the Hessian comparison theorem, let

    \[ \varphi:[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R} \]

    be a nondecreasing function. Then

    \[ \operatorname{Hess}\bigl(\varphi(\rho_1)\bigr)(X_1,X_1) \le \operatorname{Hess}\bigl(\varphi(\rho_2)\bigr)(X_2,X_2). \]

    Theorem (Laplacian Comparison Theorem)
    Edit

    Let \(M_1\) be an \(m\)-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold, and let

    \[ \gamma_1:[0,r]\to M_1 \]

    be a normal geodesic such that \(\gamma_1(r)\) is not conjugate to \(\gamma_1(0)\). Let \(\rho_1\) denote the distance function on \(M_1\) from \(\gamma_1(0)\).

    Suppose that the radial Ricci curvature of \(M_1\) along \(\gamma_1\) satisfies

    \[ \operatorname{Ric}^{M_1}\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\right) \ge (m-1)K_0. \]

    If \(K_0>0\), assume in addition that

    \[ r<\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{K_0}}. \]

    Then

    \begin{equation}\label{3} (\Delta \rho_1)\bigl(\gamma_1(r)\bigr) \le (m-1)\frac{f'(r)}{f(r)}, \end{equation}

    where \(f\) is defined as in \eqref{1}.

    Remark
    Edit

    Note that \eqref{3} holds at every smooth point of \(\rho _1\), say, if \(\gamma_1 (r)\) is not in the cut locus of \(\gamma _1(0)\). In weak sense, \eqref{3} holds globally.

    Note that for a composite function \(\varphi(\rho)\), we have

    \[ \Delta \varphi(\rho) = \varphi''(\rho) + \varphi'(\rho)\Delta \rho. \]

    Hence we obtain the following consequence.

    Corollary
    Edit

    Under the same assumptions as in the Laplacian comparison theorem, let

    \[ \varphi:[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R} \]

    be a nondecreasing function. Then

    \[ \bigl(\Delta \varphi(\rho_1)\bigr)\bigl(\gamma_1(r)\bigr) \le \varphi''(r) + (m-1)\varphi'(r)\frac{f'(r)}{f(r)}. \]

    Corollary
    Edit

    Let \(M\) be an \(m\)-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold whose Ricci curvature satisfies

    \[ \operatorname{Ric}\ge -(m-1)k^2, \qquad k\ge 0. \]

    Then, at every point where the distance function \(\rho\) is smooth,

    \[ \Delta \rho \le \frac{m-1}{\rho}(1+k\rho). \]

    Proof
    Edit

    By the Laplacian comparison theorem and the formula for the model function in the case

    \[ K_0=-k^2, \]

    we have

    \[ \Delta \rho \le (m-1)k\frac{\cosh(k\rho)}{\sinh(k\rho)}. \]

    For \(x>0\), consider the function

    \[ F(x) = (1+x)\sinh x-x\cosh x. \]

    Clearly,

    \[ F(0)=0, \]

    and

    \[ F'(x) = \sinh x+x(\cosh x-\sinh x) \ge 0. \]

    Therefore,

    \[ F(x)\ge 0, \]

    which is equivalent to

    \[ \frac{\cosh x}{\sinh x} \le \frac{1+x}{x}. \]

    Applying this inequality with \(x=k\rho\) gives

    \[ \Delta \rho \le (m-1)k\frac{\cosh(k\rho)}{\sinh(k\rho)} \le \frac{m-1}{\rho}(1+k\rho). \]
